sources.title: Visa and Passport: Entry requirements to Cuba
sources.officialityEvidence: The current Cuban tourism portal publishes entry documentation, the named Chinese ordinary-passport exemption, tourist-visa duration and the electronic visa issuance route.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Chinese nationals will not need a visa to enter Cuba with their regular passport.

sources.title: General information about Cuba
sources.publisher: Consular Department, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation
sources.officialityEvidence: The current Russian Foreign Ministry Consular Department country-information page directly states the Cuban entry rule for Russian citizens and distinguishes employment or stays over 90 days.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Въезд на Кубу для граждан России ... до 90 дней, осуществляется без визы.

sources.title: Cuba
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Serbia
sources.officialityEvidence: The current Serbian Foreign Ministry Cuba advisory expressly separates national passports from diplomatic and official passports and directs national-passport travellers to Cuba’s web visa route.
sources.supportingExcerpt: For holders of national passports and other travel documents: Visas required.

policies.title: Chinese ordinary passports: visa-free tourist entry
policies.summary: Cuba Travel expressly exempts Chinese nationals using regular passports from the tourist-visa requirement.
conditions: This is limited to Chinese nationals using regular passports for the ordinary short-tourist baseline. Cuba Travel states a tourist may stay up to 90 days, extendable once for 90 more days.

A valid passport, D’VIAJEROS QR code, medical insurance, transport and final admission requirements remain applicable. Work, residence, transit, special passports and individual restrictions are outside this policy.

policies.title: Russian ordinary passports: visa-free stays up to 90 days
policies.summary: Russia’s current Foreign Ministry consular guidance says Russian citizens may enter Cuba without a visa for a stay not exceeding 90 days using a foreign passport.
conditions: The cited bilateral-consular guidance limits visa-free travel to stays not exceeding 90 days. Longer stays, residence, employment and commercial activity require a Cuban Embassy visa.

This treats the Russian foreign passport as the ordinary-passport baseline; it does not establish special documents, dual-citizenship treatment, entry conditions, public-order controls or final admission.

policies.title: Serbian ordinary passports: electronic tourist visa required
policies.summary: Serbia’s current Foreign Ministry advisory says national passports require a Cuban visa through eVisaCuba; Cuba’s official tourism portal confirms the electronic tourist visa is issued by internet and sent as a visa code.
conditions: The Serbian MFA expressly distinguishes national passports, which require a visa, from diplomatic and official passports, which have a separate waiver.

Cuba Travel describes the issued eVisa code and states the tourist visa is single-entry for up to 90 days, extendable once for 90 more days. A valid passport, return ticket, D’VIAJEROS QR code, insurance and final admission remain required.
This is a tourist route only and does not cover work, residence, transit, emergency, diplomatic, official, service or special-document treatment.

application.label: eVisa-Cuba tourist visa portal
application.processingTime: Cuba Travel describes issuance of a visa code by email; the Serbian MFA directs national-passport applicants to the web route.
steps: Confirm that the journey is an ordinary tourist visit and that all passport and travel conditions are met.
Apply through the eVisa-Cuba route identified by Cuban and Serbian official guidance.
Use the issued visa code with the required D’VIAJEROS entry form and travel documents when seeking entry.
